citations.description: Ticket status is in_progress; ticket comments contain only problem description and recommendations, no attestation of a successful live CI run with a run ID or log URL.

findings.criterion: the full `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite runs in the GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job with ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`, confirmed by reading that job's log — not the overall run status
findings.detail: This criterion requires evidence of a live CI run completing without UserTokenLimitExceededException. The ticket is still in_progress and the comments contain only problem descriptions and recommendations — no attestation of a successful live run (no run ID, log URL, or observed outcome). The criterion is untagged so it is codebase-verifiable by default, but the outcome of a live CI job cannot be verified from the codebase. No attestation with a verifiable specific (run ID, log URL, timestamp) is recorded in the ticket.
findings.remediation: Run the GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job after merging the fix, then record a ticket comment naming the specific run ID/URL, the observed absence of UserTokenLimitExceededException in the log, and the date — so the attestation can be evaluated.

citations.description: Ticket status is in_progress; no live CI run attestation with run ID, log URL, or test count observation is present in any ticket comment.

findings.criterion: headroom is structural, not coincidental: because consumption is O(1) in test count, the run above passes with MORE live tests present than the count that first triggered the cap
findings.detail: This criterion depends on the same live CI run as AC2 — it requires observing that the run succeeded with more live tests than the ~10 that triggered the cap. No such run has been attested in the ticket. The ticket is in_progress with no live-run evidence recorded.
findings.remediation: After the live CI run passes, record a ticket comment noting the run ID/URL, the number of live tests that ran (confirming it exceeds the original cap-triggering count), and the date.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: for each one, decide whether the work is genuinely incomplete or simply undocumented. If a requirement is already satisfied but the proof is not discoverable from the code alone, add a comment to this ticket that documents the evidence — cite the concrete artifacts that meet the requirement (file paths and line ranges, commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the work to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. For any criterion whose work is genuinely unfinished, complete it, then re-verify.
